description: Off-shell follow-up to the qbk2 gate (PR #2530). Verifies the q-Bessel Green's-function kernel is a genuine propagator and that the coincidence-limit propagator G(w)=g1 g2/D is REGULAR at the substrate origin (the 2nd-kind w^{-nu} singularity cancels against the Casoratian), so the owner's 'quadratic action' is the channel in which the 2nd kind survives on-shell as a bilinear -- distinct from the linear exclusion of PR #2530. Structural identification only; no binding number (needs a physical source + cross-anchor gate). No fit; nothing wired; TIERED.
discipline: formalize-first; no fit; derive-or-refute; TIERED; nothing wired; binding-correction claim OPEN
verdict: OFF-SHELL FOLLOW-UP (formalize-first; no fit; nothing wired). The q-Bessel Green's-function kernel K(w,w')=g1(w_<)g2(w_>)/D(w') is a genuine 2-point propagator (A), and its q-Casoratian normalisation D(w)~(q^{-nu}-1)w^{-nu} (B). HEADLINE (C): the coincidence-limit propagator G(w)=g1(w)g2(w)/D(w) is REGULAR at the substrate origin (finite limit 1/(q^{-nu}-1)) -- the w^{-nu} singularity of the 2nd-kind g2 cancels against the w^{-nu} of the Casoratian D. So the QUADRATIC (bilinear) 2nd-kind object is origin-admissible even though the LINEAR g2 is not: the owner's 'quadratic action' names exactly the channel in which the 2nd kind survives on-shell, distinct from (not contradicting) the linear matrix-coefficient exclusion of PR #2530. (D) reports its bar-parity numerically. SCOPE: this is a STRUCTURAL identification of the admissible quadratic object, NOT a binding number -- a falsifiable correction still needs the physical source the propagator contracts against PLUS the cross-anchor gate (substrate-fixed coupling, no per-anchor refit). Those remain open; nothing wired; c_k/Delta_lambda stay cal-anchored. TIERED: (A)(B)(C) PROVED; the binding-correction claim is OPEN.
